prototype_assumptions: Laboratory cutting mill of the Retsch SM 300 class (160 kg, 3 kW motor, ~2 kW average; Retsch datasheet) fine-milling sawdust and seagrass in the studio at ~3 kg/h (Claude estimate for batch milling); ~5,000 h lifetime (studio use).
scaled_up_assumptions: Medium industrial biomass hammer mill (~1.5 t, 30 kW, ~1 t/h, i.e. 30 kWh/t within the 25-60 kWh/t range of the Lansonmachines hammer mill guide); 30,000 h.

prototype_assumptions: ~30 L spiral/planetary paste mixer of the bakery/studio type (120 kg, 1.5 kW, ~10 kg batches, ~10 kg/h); typical catalogue values, not retrieved online; 5,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: ~500 L industrial paddle/twin-shaft batch mixer (~1 t, 11 kW, two 0.5 t batches per hour = 1 t/h); Claude assumption; 30,000 h.

prototype_assumptions: Studio ABB robot arm (IRB 4600 class, weight from memory as the datasheet was blocked) with controller and a WASP continuous paste feeder + LDM XL extruder (5 L/h; 3dwasp.com): ~650 kg, ~2 kW, ~5 kg/h of wet paste; 10,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: Same robot with a high-flow LDM XXL-type extruder (up to 180 L/h; WASP), limited by robot path speed: 12 x 6 mm bead at 100 mm/s = ~30 kg/h, ~700 kg, 2.5 kW; 36,000 h (robot LCA, Robotics 2021).

prototype_assumptions: ~1 m3 electric convection oven modelled on the Memmert UF1060 (252 kg, 7 kW connected, ~4 kW average; memmert.com); output ~5 kg/h from an energy balance (evaporating 0.5 kg water per kg wet paste at ~40% efficiency); 10,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: Industrial ~10 m3 electric convection batch oven with better insulation (~3 t, ~30 kW, ~60 kg/h at ~65% efficiency); Claude assumption; 40,000 h.

prototype_assumptions: Small hemp/flax bast-fibre line at an existing textile mill (opening, carding, drawing and roving frames): ~3 t, 12 kW, ~15 kg/h (0.8 kWh/kg); engineering estimates anchored on textile specific-energy data, no datasheet; 50,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: Not scaled: the prototype already runs on an industrial line.

prototype_assumptions: Wet ring-spinning frame for bast fibre (~50-100 spindles) at an existing mill: ~1.5 t, 5 kW, ~6 kg/h of coarse hemp yarn (~0.83 kWh/kg, anchored on Textile School ring-spinning energy data); 50,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: Not scaled: the prototype already runs on an industrial line.

prototype_assumptions: Electronic flat-bed CNC knitting machine of the Stoll CMS class (127 cm width, 3 systems; Stoll CMS 530 page) in a fabrication lab: ~1.2 t, ~2 kW, ~1.5 kg/h (~4 m2/h at 0.4 kg/m2); 15,000 h (lab use).
scaled_up_assumptions: Wider (~244 cm) multi-system flat-bed knitting machine in a knitting mill (1,900 kg, Exapro listing; 3 kW, ~5 kg/h, 0.6 kWh/kg); 50,000 h.

prototype_assumptions: Partners' self-made sensing unit: a 10 x 15 cm box with a camera and a Raspberry-Pi-class computer that estimates roving strength by computer vision as the roving passes at ~0.2 m/s (~1 kg, ~5 W, ~4.1 kg/h of composite); Claude estimates from the partners' description; 10,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: Industrial machine-vision camera with an edge computer (~5 kg, ~30 W) at 0.5 m/s (~10 kg/h); Claude assumption; 25,000 h.

prototype_assumptions: KUKA KR210-class robot (1,111 kg, Exapro listing, + end-effector) winding one impregnated hemp roving at ~0.2 m/s (set by the sensor), with a hand-sized peristaltic resin pump (10 ml/m, partners); power 0.67 kW interpolated from Di Bari et al. 2026 (0.61 kW at 0.041 m/s, 0.85 kW at 1.0 m/s); ~4.1 kg/h; 36,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: Same robot at 0.5 m/s (0.74 kW, ~10 kg/h); Claude assumption.

prototype_assumptions: Di Bari et al. 2026 custom curing oven (7.5 x 2 x 2.4 m, U = 0.135 W/m2K, ~3 t estimated), 8 h at 80 C: ~0.61 kW wall loss, ~1.4 kg/h calibrated to the paper's 0.91e-2 MJ per m of roving; 30,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: Same oven and profile; the paper's value already assumes a full oven, so prototype and scaled-up are identical.

prototype_assumptions: Medical/lab X-ray CT scanner (partners) scanning 3-4 pieces at once at 1 min per 2 m: ~2.5 t, ~10 kW average (mostly idle; Heye et al. 2020 hospital CT energy data), ~940 kg/h; ~20,000 h (medical CTs are replaced after ~10 y).
scaled_up_assumptions: Industrial multi-sensor lumber scanner of the MiCROTEC Goldeneye class (X-ray + 3D laser, EN 14081 strength grading, 150-1,200 m/min; microtec.com): ~10 t and ~50 kW (Claude estimates), ~10,000 kg/h; 60,000 h.

prototype_assumptions: ABB IRB 6620 robot (900 kg, ABB datasheet) with a Zivid 3D camera scanning each piece for warp/twist in a few seconds (partners); ~1 min per piece incl. handling = ~360 kg/h, ~1.5 kW; 36,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: Same robot and camera with automated feeding (0.25 min per piece, ~1,450 kg/h); in a real plant this would merge with the industrial scanner, which already measures 3D geometry.

prototype_assumptions: Martin T54-class surface planer in the partners' workshop (1,200 kg, 5.5 kW motor, ~4 kW average; hoechsmann.com listing) doing all the planing: 5 m/min feed (partners: 2-8 m/min), ~4 passes of 3 mm = ~170 kg/h; yield 80% (60-92%) from the partners' 10-40% loss and their planing image; 30,000 h.
scaled_up_assumptions: Weinig Powermat 1500 four-sided moulder (4,100 kg, 73 kW installed, 5-40 m/min; werktuigen.com listing) planing all faces in one pass at ~20 m/min, ~30 kW average, ~2,680 kg/h; 60,000 h.

prototype_assumptions: Same ABB IRB 6620 robot with a drilling spindle drilling ~25 mm dowel holes through the stacked beam (2 per m of span); ~1 min per hole (Claude estimate from wood drilling feeds; partners gave up to 10 min), ~1.5 kW, ~410 kg/h; 36,000 h. Assembly (hammering in dowels) is manual and has no machine.
scaled_up_assumptions: Hundegger K2i-class beam processing centre (24,000 kg, werktuigen.com listing; ~15 kW average, Claude estimate) at ~0.2 min per hole, ~2,050 kg/h; 60,000 h.
